name: Guillotine Defense and Escape
description: Defend and escape a guillotine choke by protecting the neck, clearing the choking arm, and recovering to a neutral or dominant position.
shortInstruction: Tuck your chin, hand fight the choking arm, stack your weight onto them, and peel the arm across your body to escape.
summary: Guillotine defense uses chin tuck, hand fighting, and body position to relieve neck pressure, then a systematic sequence to clear the choking arm and recover guard or top position. The system prioritizes posture and arm control over explosive yanking.
whyItWorks: Tucking the chin closes the space between your neck and shoulder, making it harder for the choking arm to sink deep
Controlling the choking arm at the elbow (not the hand) gives you mechanical advantage — the elbow is the fulcrum of the choke
Stacking your weight forward onto the opponent loads their upper back and forces them to carry your body weight, making them drop the choke attempt
Peeling the arm across your body uses your entire torso rotation, not just arm strength, to break the grip
commonMistakes: Looking up (extending the neck) as you feel the choke — this opens the throat and deepens the guillotine
Grabbing the hand instead of the arm — a hand grip can be peeled but the arm control prevents them from re-sinking
Trying to bench press or extend the arms away from the body — this raises your posture and deepens the choke
Staying flat on your stomach when the guillotine is locked — this gives them all the leverage and no escape route
coachingCues: Control the elbow, not the hand
safetySummary: The guillotine can cause unconsciousness in seconds if the carotid arteries are compressed — tap early if the choke is deep
Some guillotine variations target the trachea rather than the carotid — this is more dangerous and should be tapped to immediately
Do not fight a deep guillotine — it is better to tap, reset, and try the defense earlier in the next engagement
Neck cranks disguised as guillotines (pressure on the chin instead of the throat) require immediate tapping to protect the cervical spine

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The guillotine defense follows a three-phase sequence: prevention → defense → escape

decisionTree.action: as you enter the takedown or front headlock, keep your chin tucked and your head slightly to one side. Do not lead with your forehead straight into their chest
if they lock the guillotine, immediately freeze and chin tuck. Both hands go to their choking arm at the elbow. Do not bridge or spaz — posture first
stack your weight forward by walking your knees toward their head. As their back touches the mat, peel the choking arm across your body using your forearm rotation
Escape branch: if they roll to guard during the escape, keep their sleeve controlled and post up into their guard. If they stand up, release the grip and circle to neutral

moneyDetails: The guillotine is the most common submission from failed takedowns and front headlocks — a reliable defense is essential for every grappler
Mastering the guillotine defense allows you to shoot takedowns without fear of being caught in the most common counter
A smooth guillotine escape often leads directly to a dominant top position (passing their open guard as they post up)
fixItFast: If they have a high-wrist guillotine (deep chin strap): do not try to peel the grip — instead, post your hand on their hip, drive your head to the outside, and circle out
If they drop to guard with the guillotine: keep your posture tall, hands on their hip (not their choking arm), and drive your trapped shoulder into their thigh
If they switch to an anaconda or D'Arce: frame on their head with your free arm and drive your shoulder into their chest before they can lock the figure-four
